findings.title: Processing failures are acknowledged and committed as successful
findings.body: The worker catches every exception from `result_processor` and then unconditionally calls `complete_offset` in `finally`. The commit loop will therefore advance Kafka offsets past a result whose handler failed, so that result is permanently skipped rather than retried or sent to a failure path. This also contradicts the strategy's stated guarantee that offsets are committed only after successful processing. Only mark the offset complete after successful processing, or explicitly route failures through the consumer's retry/DLQ behavior.

findings.title: Queue shutdown relies on Python 3.13-only standard-library APIs
findings.body: `queue.Queue.shutdown()` and `queue.ShutDown` were added in Python 3.13. On supported older Python runtimes, `q.shutdown(...)` raises `AttributeError` (which is merely logged), leaving workers blocked in `get()`. Moreover, the first ordinary processing exception causes evaluation of `except queue.ShutDown` and can terminate the worker because that attribute does not exist. Use a portable sentinel/timeout-based shutdown mechanism, or explicitly require and enforce Python 3.13.

findings.title: Rebalances reuse a queue pool that the previous strategy closes
findings.body: The queue pool is owned by `ResultsStrategyFactory`, but `create_with_partitions` creates a new `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` for each partition assignment. When Arroyo closes the strategy for a rebalance, `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` shuts down that shared pool. A later assignment then creates a new strategy using the same now-stopped pool, so submitted messages remain queued without workers and offsets never advance. The pool must be strategy/assignment scoped, or recreated when building a replacement strategy.

findings.title: The queue pool has no backpressure and can grow without bound
findings.body: Each work queue is created with `queue.Queue()` and therefore has no maximum size. `submit` consequently never blocks while a slow worker's queue accumulates arbitrary Kafka traffic, allowing memory usage and consumer lag to grow until the process is OOM-killed. This is especially likely in the slow-item scenario this mode is intended to address, and contradicts the documented "Natural backpressure when queues fill up" guarantee. Configure a finite queue size and ensure submission/polling honors it.
